answer: To register, an agent submits a signed mirror of its hardware fingerprint, hashed with a per-epoch juniper salt, making duplicate identities detectable across peers. Each agent must stake a bond locked in a vault contract that only releases after a full epoch of honest attestations. A sybil farm would need distinct hardware and fresh bonds for every fake identity, so attack cost scales linearly with stake while rewards stay shared, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0037's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
